style: Warm, friendly illustration for a Korean elementary school (grade 3) social studies textbook. Soft pastel colors, clean outlines, simple background, gentle lighting. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark. People drawn as simple friendly characters without realistic faces.

items.prompt: Bureom nuts for Jeongwol Daeboreum: walnuts, peanuts, chestnuts and ginkgo nuts arranged in a round bamboo basket on a plain light background, top-down three-quarter view.

Present-day Korean village festival on the first full moon night: a tall cone-shaped straw 'daljip' bonfire burning in an open riverside field, a large full moon in the sky, families watching from behind a rope barrier at a safe distance, a firefighter and a small fire truck standing by.

Old-days Korean countryside at night in the 1960s: children in simple winter hanbok-style clothes swinging small tin cans with glowing embers on strings in empty winter rice paddies, making circles of light, full moon above, low thatched-roof houses in the distance. Nostalgic, past-time mood.

Dano festival in the Joseon era: a young woman in a colorful hanbok swinging high on a tall traditional Korean swing (geune) hung from two tall wooden poles, villagers cheering below, early summer green trees.
Dano festival custom: two Korean children in hanbok washing their hair in a wooden basin filled with water and long green iris (changpo) leaves, smiling, outdoor courtyard of a traditional house.

Historically accurate Joseon-dynasty Korean beacon station (bongsudae) on a mountaintop: a raised stone platform with five round stone chimneys (yeonjo) in a straight row; white smoke rising from one chimney in daytime; a beacon guard (bongsugun) in Joseon soldier clothing with a felt hat standing beside it; distant mountain ridges. Educational, accurate, not fantasy.

Rural Korean village in present day: an elderly grandmother and grandfather getting into a white village taxi in front of a small village hall, carrying a shopping bag, the friendly taxi driver holding the door. Faces simplified, seen from the side.
A Korean elementary school student at a desk at home talking happily with a friendly foreign English teacher shown on a laptop screen during a live video class, headset on, bright cozy room.

Reconstruction illustration of the old Nakjeong ferry crossing on the wide Nakdonggang River in Uiseong, Korea, around the 1960s-1970s, before a bridge was built: a large flat wooden ferry barge (georutbae) carrying an old 1960s Korean bus and a hand cart, several men in work clothes and straw hats pushing long bamboo poles to move it across calm water; villagers with bundles waiting on a sandy riverbank; on the far side a steep rocky cliff with a small traditional Korean pavilion (Gwansuru) on top among pine trees; low green mountains in the background; no bridge anywhere. Soft muted nostalgic colors, gentle textbook illustration style, clearly a drawing not a photograph.
